$comment: The Buginese block, as encoded. This file holds script and encoding FACTS — codepoints, Unicode character names, block metadata — not orthographic rules. Orthography lives in rules.json. `pnpm rules:validate` checks every codepoint and unicodeName here against the vendored font's cmap, so a transcription slip fails the build.

source.citation: Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf, block Buginese; 30 assigned code points since Unicode 4.1 (2005)
source.designRationale: Everson, encoding proposals L2/98-021, L2/99-011, L2/03-191, L2/03-320

block.viramaNote: There is no virama in the block. Consequently there is no mechanism in the encoding for a bare consonant, and the four lossy classes in rules.json follow from that absence.

inherentVowel.note: Every consonant letter carries the inherent vowel /a/. A vowel sign replaces it; there is no way to remove it.

order.name: ka-ga-nga
order.note: The codepoint order U+1A00..U+1A16 is the traditional order. The on-screen keyboard is laid out in it, in rows of four, which is how the code chart itself groups the letters.

$vowelSignComment: generalCategory and combiningClass are read from the UCD and are facts. `position` is derived from the combining class where the UCD determines one, and is 'unverified' where it does not — E and O are spacing marks (Mc), so they take advance width, but which side they sit on is a rendering question answered by the conformance page, not something to assert here.

vowelSigns.positionSource: Spacing combining mark; the UCD assigns no combining class. See the rendering conformance page.
Spacing combining mark; the UCD assigns no combining class. See the rendering conformance page.
Non-spacing mark, but the UCD assigns no combining class. See the rendering conformance page.
vowelSigns.latinNote: `ae` is taken from the Unicode character name, not from a Bugis Latin orthography. Which Latin letter or diacritic this sign corresponds to is an open question — see the ejaan page.

$punctuationComment: `latin` is deliberately null for both marks. The function of pallawa in Bugis practice, and how either mark should be represented in Latin, is not something this repo can cite yet — see the ejaan page. Presenting a guess as the answer is the specific failure this project must avoid.
